title: WB2A controlled E7=100 high-flow heating comparison

authorization.user_action: Opened several radiators and authorized temporary E7=100 for a normal heating observation.

precondition.note: Probe intentionally waited while DHW was active. No E7 write occurred until DHW=0 and flame=0.

immediate_effect.interpretation: A1 runtime request, final internal-pump setpoint and physical internal-pump speed all followed the temporary E7=100 setting immediately.

heating_cycle.termination_note: The user later switched the operating mode back to DHW-only. The cycle therefore must be treated as a lower-bound runtime observation, not a natural full-cycle duration.
heating_cycle.comparison: The E7=100/high-flow heating run remained continuously in flame for at least 391 s, whereas the preceding E7=30 baseline complete flame runs lasted 33.9-41.5 s.

helper.issue: The recorder stopped advancing its CSV around 12:00 while its process remained alive. Independent read-only control snapshots were therefore used for the remainder of the observation. The helper was force-terminated before manual controlled restore. Root cause not yet established.

established: Temporary E7=100 caused the A1 runtime request to become 100%, with 0x0A3C and 0x7660[1] both following to 100%.
With multiple radiators opened and pump flow at 100%, boiler temperature was drawn down enough to allow a substantially longer burner run.
The burner remained continuously active for at least 391 s and modulated down to about 33% near the heating target.
This contrasts strongly with the preceding E7=30 baseline, where complete flame runs were approximately 34-42 s and flame-off intervals approximately 248 s.
Normal flame cycling itself does not drive the pump result; pump request/result remained invariant through the baseline takt cycles.
not_established: Because heat-emitter load was intentionally changed by opening radiators, the longer burner run cannot be attributed to E7 alone.
Because the user ended heating mode before natural flame-off was observed, no natural E7=100 burner-cycle duration is claimed.
No conclusion is made that E7=100 is an appropriate permanent setting.
interpretation.value_for_research: The experiment confirms the request/result topology and provides a high-flow reference state for future pump and combustion dynamics comparisons.

interpretation_correction_2026_09_25.note: Raw measurements remain valid. The earlier wording that E7 -> A1 runtime request -> 0x0A3C -> physical internal pump represented one causal chain was too coarse. Direct A1 heating, DHW/internal-pump operation and boiler-circuit operation are distinct logical roles of the integrated pump. E7 is the direct-A1 regulated heating-circuit-pump minimum; 6C controls the internal pump in DHW; K31 applies to the boiler-circuit role. 0x0A3C/0x7660 correlations are retained as observations but are not used as proof of direct-A1 control topology.
interpretation_correction_2026_09_25.production_decision: Do not implement burner-triggered E7 writes as the solution. Continue searching for a source-backed internal burner-dependent A1 pump function or firmware/runtime state.
